gaps.note: The BDM2/BDM2m datasheet states "Total Power 300 W" in a technical specifications table headed "BDM2/2 m with 6+12 IO Card", whose RF connector row describes that card's six downstream and twelve upstream ports. The figure is the assembly's. A BDM position is TWO modules here - casa/bdm in a front bay and casa/io-6p12 in the paired rear bay, which is why casa/bdm already carries `pairs-with` - and no document we hold divides the 300 W between them. Writing it onto the front module would make the chassis total come out right and the answer to "what does a BDM front module draw" come out wrong, so neither half carries a figure and the chassis total stays a floor. The arithmetic does not settle it either way: 12 x 300 W lands on the C100G's stated 3.6 kW whether the 300 W is the pair or the front half with small rear cards. The C100G HIG corroborates the assembly reading and hedges it: Tables A-10 and A-11 both read "Approximately 300W per BDM" under titles scoping them to the BDM WITH its 6+12 I/O. THE LIBRARY IS CURRENTLY INCONSISTENT ABOUT THIS, ON PURPOSE AND VISIBLY. The three BDM variants carry NO power figure, for the reason above. The DQM and DCU cards added later DO carry one - DS8x8 220, DS8x96 320, DS8x192 350, US16x8 220, US16x4 150 - each with a `power-scope` provenance entry saying in the vendor's own words that the number covers the card WITH its I/O module and must not have a rear figure added to it. Both are defensible readings of the same problem: one keeps the per-module answer honest and the chassis total a floor, the other keeps the vendor's only published number reachable. They should not stay different once a pairing-scoped mechanism exists, and this is the record of which way each went and why, so that whoever unifies them is not guessing. THE THREE REAR RF I/O CARDS ADDED LATER FALL ON THE SAME SIDE OF THIS AS THE 6+12. casa/rfd, casa/rfu-16x8 and casa/ups-32x4 carry NO power figure, because Tables A-8 and A-9 give their port counts and connector types and no watts at all, and every figure Casa does publish for the slot is already the pair's - Table A-3 heads the DQM column "Maximum consumption with I/O module" and Table A-4 gives "Single DCU w/ RFU I/O" 200 W against "Single DCU w/ RFU UPS 32x4 I/O" 220 W for the same US16x8. Subtracting one from the other to get a rear card's share would be our arithmetic and would also be the wrong subtraction - the 20 W is the difference between two PAIRINGS, not between two I/O cards.
gaps.wanted: a pairable unit that can carry properties, so that a figure measured on a pair can be attached to the pair. The scope is now DATA - every card here declares `power-draw-scope: module-with-paired-io`, so a chassis sum knows not to add the rear partner and L30 catches it if one gains its own figure - but the scope says only THAT the figure covers a pair, not WHICH pair. The C100G HIG gives the same US16x8 200 W with the RFU I/O and 220 W with the RFU UPS 32x4, and the manifest can carry only one of them. Asking for "a per-module figure" was the wrong question: Casa states none, and one may not exist to be divided out. What is missing is the mechanism, and enough vendors doing this to design one from - Casa is the only one in the corpus.

gaps.note: The card band runs 37.5 to 386.7 in a body 432.95 wide, so it sits 37.5 from the left edge and 46.25 from the right - 8.75 mm out of centre, or 4.375 on the band's own centreline. Everything inside the band agrees with everything else; the question is whether the band is really off-centre in the metal, and nothing we hold answers it. IT IS NOT COSMETIC, and the AC input panel is where it bites. Its four C14 inlets sit behind the four front power supplies. Reflect the supply centres about the PANEL and the inlets are 1.2 out; reflect them about the CHASSIS - which is what walking round a box actually does - and they are 9.95 out. The gap between those two answers IS this asymmetry, and no arrangement of the parts inside the band can close it, because the disagreement is between the band and the chassis rather than within either. THE SUPPORTING NUMBERS ARE ALSO ODD IN THE SAME DIRECTION. The two front fan strips measure 36.0 wide each - equal, as you would expect - but leave 1.5 outside them on the left and 10.25 on the right. Two equal strips with unequal surrounds is exactly the shape of a band that has been positioned from one edge. NOT RESOLVED BY GUESSING, deliberately. Re-centring the band would move the two fan strips, the card bays on both faces, the PSU row, the PSU cover and the AC panel - and it would be one estimate reconciled against another, which this device's `pem-band-top-edge` note already records going wrong twice in opposite directions.

Its TOP edge is known only to about 2 mm, and the three candidates each have support: 194.0 is the direct reading of Figure 1-4 and is impossible, because the card slot above ends at 194.82; 194.82 is flush against that slot; 196.0 is what the bays carry and is what the manifest now uses, on the argument that 194.82 is an accumulation of six DERIVED slot pitches (426.6 mm over 14 slots on the C100G, carried across) and that the front face shows a measured 1.48 mm margin in the equivalent position. That argument is sound but it is an argument, not a measurement, and the whole disagreement is six pixels at 2.982 px/mm. A tape measure on a real C40G, or any Casa drawing that dimensions the rear panel, would settle it in one number. FIGURE 1-12 HAS NOW BEEN LOOKED AT AND DOES NOT SETTLE IT, recorded so nobody spends the search twice. "C40G power entry module" is the only isolated drawing of this part and the first independent look anything has had at it. Its body measures 866 x 381 px for an aspect of 2.273. The modelled 158.0 x 68.5 is 2.307 and the superseded 158.0 x 70.5 is 2.241, and 2.273 lands 0.04 percent off the midpoint of those two - at 158.0 wide it implies a height of 69.51. IT IS EQUIDISTANT AND CONFIRMS NEITHER. This guide's isolated part drawings are in any case demonstrably about 10 percent wrong about their own aspect - Figure 1-20 draws a card at 12.54 whose real aspect is 11.34 - so a 1.5 percent lean is well inside the drawing's own error. THE NUMBER IS THEREFORE NOT MOVED. It has been moved twice already, in both directions, and a third move on evidence that splits the difference would be the reconciliation loop rather than an escape from it. What Figure 1-12 does confirm is the ARRANGEMENT, which is what a figure is good for: a bolted terminal cover across the top with three fasteners, a minus pair of studs above a plus pair inside two outlined blocks, two release levers standing proud of the body top and bottom, and the yellow disconnect-power label to their right - all of which casa/c40g-pem draws. RECORDED BECAUSE THE MODULE AND THE BAY NOW AGREE, which means nothing will ever flag this again - the fit check that found the original 2 mm discrepancy is satisfied by both being wrong together as easily as by both being right.

gaps.note: The ASR 9001-S is the same metal as the ASR 9001 with two of its four fixed SFP+ ports disabled until a licence is applied. That is not a population fact - the cages are physically present and identical - so `bays:` cannot express it, and the ports are correctly drawn present in both configurations. INVESTIGATED AND IT DOES NOT REACH: `component-attrs` is the closest mechanism the format has, and it is keyed by component NAME rather than by placement id. render.py computes `comp_name = ref.split("/")[-1].split("@")[0]` and looks the overrides up by that, so `component-attrs: {sfp-ganged: ...}` would mark all SIX std/sfp-ganged instances on this chassis - both CLUSTER ports and all four SFP+ - when only two are disabled. A placement can carry `attrs:` per instance but not per configuration; `component-attrs` is per configuration but not per instance. The 9001-S needs both at once and neither mechanism spans the gap. The same edge stops this configuration carrying its own 60 Gbps fabric figure, since a configuration cannot override device attrs at all.
gaps.wanted: per-instance attrs in a configuration - `component-attrs` keyed by placement id as well as by component name would do it - or a device-attrs override in a configuration. This is a second instance of the shape recorded in working/notes/config-scoped-placements.md, from a different vendor: the format can say what OCCUPIES a bay per configuration, but not what is TRUE of a part per configuration.

Three of them need 428.34 mm and this chassis's power shelf interior measures 416.50, so they do not fit - lint L13 flagged the overlap directly when they were placed at the measured centres. Against that, the stencil's shape box for the 'A9K Power Module' master reads 0.5477 in, which is 139.12 mm at the stencil's 1:10 scale, and my own measurement of the three openings in the ASR 9006 front master gives 138.35, 137.50 and 138.23. Those two agree to under a millimetre, and three at 139.12 come to 417.36 against a 416.50 shelf - the arithmetic a shelf that holds exactly three ought to produce. The 142.78 is most likely the art measured over something that is not the module's seating width, the same class of error as reading a card's shape box instead of its art. gaps.note: NINE CARDS SHARE THESE SIX SLOTS AND TWO FAMILIES DISAGREE BY 32.8 mm ON THE ONE AXIS THAT HAS TO FIT ONE OPENING. The line cards and the blank filler are 395.7 mm; all four RSP-880 variants are 428.5. The measured cage opening is 352.59. The line-card story is coherent: a9k-slot-cover's own art measures a PLATE of 362.24 inside a 395.7 envelope, so the plate covers the 352.59 opening with 4.8 mm of overlap per side and the ejector brackets account for the remaining 16.7 per side. Every number has a job. The RSP-880's does not. 428.5 needs 37.96 mm of overlap per side to cover the same opening, and a card centred on this cage reaches x 22.99 to 451.49 in a 444.5 mm chassis - 6.99 mm PAST the outer wall, which is visible in the 3D view as the card's end standing proud of the side of the box. WHERE 428.5 COMES FROM, AND WHY IT IS THE SUSPECT: the RSP-880 data sheet's 'Physical specifications' row. This library's own a9k-rsp880-se provenance already records that NINE RSP AND RP MASTERS IN THE STENCIL ARE ONE DRAWING, scaled to four different stated widths - 402.8, 428.5, 428.2 and 403.4 - so "the drawing is generic across the family and cannot be all four sizes". The cage, by contrast, is measured off this chassis's own master and independently supported by Figure 19. NOT RESOLVED HERE. Two numbers describing different things is the likeliest reading - the same trap as a plate against an envelope - but nothing we hold says WHICH thing 428.5 measures, and inventing a smaller one would be the reconciliation this project keeps digging back out.
gaps.wanted: a Cisco mechanical drawing of an RSP-880 faceplate, or one measurement across a real card from ejector tip to ejector tip. Either settles it for all four variants at once and for every chassis they go in. gaps.note: THESE BAY DIMENSIONS WERE GROWN TO MEET A COMPONENT AND ARE NOT MEASUREMENTS. Each was set by taking the size of a card the bay accepts, because a fit check reported the bay as too small. On this chassis: 403.10 on 8 bays - the 5th-generation envelope, 403.10 long 406.40 on 2 bays - a9k-rsp, 406.40 long The danger is specific and it is why they are listed rather than left to look like geometry. A fit check compares a bay to a component and NEITHER of them to the world, so it is satisfied by both being wrong together exactly as easily as by both being right. Every mismatch resolved by moving one side removes the signal without adding any truth, and once resolved nothing will flag it again. These are the entries where that happened, so the record survives the check going quiet. What IS independently grounded and is not in this list: the cage extents, measured off the stencil and confirmed on several chassis by printed slot labels or a card guide rail; the slot pitch; the 395.70 fourth-generation envelope, which is Cisco's own "includes ejector bracket/lever" figure; and the shapesheet sizes for the power modules and fan trays. gaps.note: The guide states that "line cards must be installed upside down in slots 10 through 19 of the bottom card cage, whereas in slots 0 though 9 of the top card cage, the line cards are installed right side up". This is a real property of the chassis and the model cannot currently express it. The bays for 10 to 19 are geometrically identical to 0 to 9 and carry no rotation, because the card is inverted about its own long axis rather than rotated in the plane of the panel - a `rotate: 180` would spin the faceplate end for end, which is a different thing and would put the ejectors at the wrong ends. So a card rendered in slot 15 will show its ports and its part number the same way up as one in slot 5, and on real hardware it would not. Anyone reading port positions off the lower cage should know that.
